findings.premise: Extending enforceCodeReviewGate alone prevents every existing BUILD approval route from consuming a stale fingerprinted review.
findings.evidence: The TUI approve service directly executes `const approval = approveArtifactByJsonPath(...)`. That lower-level function calls otherPartyReviewGap, whose BUILD branch reads the CR and assigns `reviewer = reviewerPartyOf(cr.meta)`; it checks existence and reviewer party, but never calls enforceCodeReviewGate. Only approveWorkflowTarget calls enforceCodeReviewGate, and its current refusal branch is `if (gate.status === 'blocked')`. Section 3.13 omits src/workflow/gates.ts from its change sites and does not extend the common approval boundary. As written, stale fingerprinted CRs can still authorize BUILD approval through the TUI. findings.premise: Incomplete capture, oversized singleton fragments and invalid parent evidence have explicit detection and failure/recovery contracts.
findings.evidence: The real reader exposes truncation and git_diff has a 256KiB default and 2MiB hard capture cap. Existing pipeline redivision repacks atom IDs; it cannot split a singleton's text. The design addresses those distinct limits through reader recovery-or-refusal, measured Unicode-safe repartition, no-progress termination and immutable revision provenance. It also requires missing parent/global notes to fail before adjudication instead of using the existing NO_EVIDENCE path. findings.premise: The design explicitly separates waiter detachment, operation cancellation, deadline expiry and unsupported bounded execution.
findings.evidence: Currently runReviewStream invokes transport.cancel on timeout/abort, and the in-daemon transport aborts its handler signal. Current code-review tokens also share one-hour TTL/LRU eviction. Sections 3.8–3.12 explicitly replace these behaviors for opted-in operations: separate operation ownership, pinned active state, immutable deadlines, terminal capability refusal, late-answer rejection and cancellation of owned execution.
